statements.quote: All conditions of the story writing task were completed on an external custom website which was accessed through an embedded link on Qualtrics.
For the AI-help condition, participants were instructed to collaborate with ChatGPT during the story writing task (Appendix A).

statements.quote: A custom API was used to call ChatGPT based on the GPT 3.5 base model. This model was selected given its widespread popularity at the time of data collection, as it was freely available from OpenAI through their domain (https://chatgpt.com/).

statements.quote: The visual features of the No-AI condition were matched to the AI-help condition, except the ChatGPT textbox was removed and only the story writing textbox was displayed, stretched horizontally to cover a larger portion of the webpage (Appendix B).
statements.locator: p. 10, Method, Story Writing Task, reference to Appendix B

statements.quote: The model is available online on the Creativity Assessment Platform (CAP) and leverages a fine-tuned LLM that was trained to predict human-rated originality scores to a large dataset of multilingual stories (Luchini et al., 2024).

Further, the MiniLM model is relatively small compared to its counterparts, with only 118 million parameters, and is openly-accessible through the SentenceTransformers Python framework on Hugging Face (Hugging Face, n.d.).
We devised a novel classification scheme to determine if prompts sent by users to the AI involve idea generation or elaboration (Appendix C).
While we report findings for our analyses with outlier removal, analyses without outlier removal led to the same conclusions (Appendix D).

deposits.notes: Project title: Naturalistic Story-Writing Co-Creativity Between Humans and AI. The exact paper/form link and canonical https://osf.io/nz6ag/ both returned HTTP 200 without authentication. The node API reports public=true. File listing, children, storage providers, wikis and linked_nodes endpoints returned HTTP 200: two files, zero child components, only OSF storage, zero wikis and zero linked nodes. CoCreativityDF.csv (https://osf.io/download/z7fjv/) and AnalysisTable.docx (https://osf.io/download/ds2vb/) both downloaded with HTTP 200 and were read in memory. CSV SHA-256: 9b26e7f7a06ce3f9eedf46344600106a5032b91417d199e60c651d531d3c3a63. One row per participant: 263 distinct IDs and 263 nonmissing observations in each primary originality, diversity-contribution, and word-count column. This is a repeated-measures design: _AIhelp and _noAI column suffixes identify condition; has_arm_assignment=true refers to these condition labels, not randomized order, which is absent. The four self-judgment/self-judgment-accuracy columns have 254 nonmissing values each, with nine NA entries; self-judgment columns also include four AI-help and three No-AI zero values despite the paper's stated 1-5 scale, so nonmissing counts alone do not establish valid analyzed counts for that outcome. No story texts, AI responses, prompt texts, prompt identities, embeddings, order variable, demographics or excluded-participant rows. Diversity columns contain the published mixed-prompt-pool contribution scores, not within-arm set diversity. AnalysisTable.docx contains aggregate results only. No analysis scripts or license were found in this project (node_license=null).

Project title: Generative AI Does Not Erase Individual Differences in Human Creativity. Found through OSF title and first-author searches, following the form's unverified sample-overlap lead. Public node, file/folder listings, children and storage-provider APIs returned HTTP 200; there are no child components, only OSF storage, and no wiki. All 19 leaf files were listed recursively: five in Study1, 13 in Study2 (including SensitivityAnalysis), and Supplemental.pdf at the root. The Study1 folder and Supplemental.pdf sections A-B concern c159 S1; all participant-data flags and rows/columns checked in this entry refer to that sample. The later preprint (https://api.osf.io/v2/preprints/jszrn_v1/; PDF https://osf.io/download/zxmwb/, both HTTP 200) explicitly states on p. 6 that Study 1 reanalyzes Luchini et al. (2025c), and its p. 35 reference identifies the c159 title. Study1/study1_ai_creativity_with_header.csv (https://osf.io/download/dgb7q/, HTTP 200; SHA-256 718992241ccbaf5c0e15e4e80a44e2398aee1ac868f1d836ffbae5adcca63d5e) has 263 distinct participant IDs and complete values in all 12 columns. The orig_ai/orig and elab_ai/elab pairs match all 263 rows of c159's AI-help/No-AI originality and word-count columns in file order. IDs are renumbered: none match the first deposit's IDs at the same row position, so a join on ID would be incorrect. The _ai suffix distinguishes AI-help from No-AI. Additional fields include age, sex codes, intelligence indicators and DSI scores; DSI is not the paper's across-person diversity-contribution measure. The Study1 CSV contains no stories, prompt texts, original diversity-contribution scores, order or prompt identity, or excluded participants. The sex code distribution is 0:235, 1:27, 3:1; code meanings were not confirmed and are not assigned gender labels here. All five Study1 files and the two-page Supplemental.pdf were read in memory (HTTP 200). The R and Mplus files implement the later reanalysis, not c159's primary analysis. Despite its name, study1_ai_creativity_noheader.csv contains an X1-X12 header followed by 263 data rows and uses different IDs again; rows_checked and columns_checked refer to the explicit-header file. Supplemental.pdf p. 1 supplies the Study 1 LLM system prompt and brainstorming instructions, not participant responses. Study2 files concern a different sample and are not evidence that c159 story texts are available. No dataset license was found (node_license=null).

what_we_could_compute: S1-O1: condition-specific participant means, sample SDs, SEs, complete analyzed counts, paired-difference SD/SE and within-person correlation. This resolves final.open_items' 'SD = 08' ambiguity using data: sample SD = 0.08365611497212164 for AI-help and 0.08460153812832794 for No-AI, each n=263 (computed from the public CSV, not quoted from the PDF).

S1-O2: means, SDs, SEs, analyzed counts and paired comparisons for the already computed diversity-contribution scores in CoCreativityDF.csv. These are contributions to mixed-condition prompt pools; neither deposit permits new within-arm set-diversity calculations because c159's texts, embeddings and prompt assignments are absent.

The confidence-interval/effect-size open item can be checked by recomputing paired mean-difference CIs and d_z from the observed paired scores. Reproduction can establish numerical consistency but cannot confirm an unstated author definition.

The prompt-count outlier open item can be checked by rerunning correlations and partial correlations with originality/diversity difference scores and word-count differences. Applying the stated mean plus three sample SD rule to the posted counts removes two generation observations (261 retained) and seven elaboration observations (256 retained); these are calculations from the data, not replacement quotations for conflicting printed dfs.

Outcome-specific nonmissing counts and self-assessment summaries can be computed. The self-assessment columns contain NA and out-of-range zero values, so any valid-case rule must be explicit rather than assuming all 263 were analyzed for these outcomes.

The related Study1 deposit permits direct counts of sex codes and age summaries for the same 263 participants. Sex codes have counts 235, 27 and 1, but the checked files do not establish category labels, so the paper's gender-count discrepancy is not conclusively resolved.
notes: Checked 2026-10-09. The entire supplied markdown was read in chunks (444 lines), including references and Appendices A-D, and the availability/materials passages were checked against the 34-page PDF with PyMuPDF. Quotes reproduce PDF wording with line-wrap whitespace normalized. The only explicit study-data availability statement in the saved paper is the OSF statement on p. 8; no preregistration statement, separate online supplement link, or study-specific code-release statement was found. The other quoted passages point to embedded materials or software used. The PsyArXiv landing page https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/xm2f5_v3 returned HTTP 200, redirecting to https://osf.io/xm2f5_v3; its HTML is a JavaScript shell. The public preprint API also returned HTTP 200 and names the same nz6ag data link, has_prereg_links='no', and no journal DOI. The preprint file listing contains only Human-AI Collaborative Creativity.pdf (1004127 bytes), not separate supplementary data. Its versions endpoint lists v1-v3, all with the same data link; its latest-version flag is inconsistent with numeric version order, so the supplied v3 remains the source of record. Confidence is high for verified participant-data availability; it does not assert an exhaustive absence of deposits on the internet. Broad surname/topic searches were refined and search failures are recorded rather than treated as zero matches. Both useful deposits provide scored participant data but neither supplies c159's story texts, randomized sequence, story-prompt identity, or the 128 removed participants. Thus carryover/order effects, exclusions by order, original assignment counts, and new within-arm text diversity remain unavailable. Duplicate deposits reuse one sample and must not be counted as independent studies. No authentication, account creation or access requests were used. No data files were saved to disk. Other paper/PDF URL checks (background references, software and citation artifacts, not c159 deposits): https://chatgpt.com/ -> HTTP 403; https://doi-org.leo.lib.unomaha.edu/10.1177/0018720811411912 -> HTTP status null (URLError: <urlopen error [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1028)>); https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.93.5.880 -> HTTP 403; https://doi.org/10.31219/osf.io/fgqcz_v1 -> HTTP 200; https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/8p9wu -> HTTP 200; https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/bw87y -> HTTP 200; https://huggingface.co -> HTTP 200; https://www.sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/pretrained_models.html -> HTTP 200; https://www.zotero.org/google-docs/?nSrOPj -> HTTP 200.
